sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Ulm has used resident permits to restrict parking around its centre, in two steps. On 16 February 2022 the council raised the annual fee from €30 to €200 by 20 votes to 19, with the administration having proposed €300 [0]. From 1 February 2026 it rose to €300, when new 'Mischparken' began in areas next to the centre. Permit holders park without a time limit, and others need a ticket or disc on weekdays from 9:00 to 20:00, with a four-hour maximum [1]. Only parts of Zone F (Neustadt) became paid at once. In the other new zones, disc parking stays free for four hours until meters are installed [2]. Meters in the centre cost €2.50 an hour, and the city has said this is to rise to €3 in the coming year [3].

The city also wants fewer surface spaces in the old town. It counts about 1,500 above-ground spaces in the old-town ring and has said it aims to move them into the garages, while the chamber of commerce has criticised lost parking from new pedestrian zones [18]. The Umweltzone was abolished on 4 June 2024 [24]. A 2021 mobility programme prioritised the S-Bahn, mobility stations and cycle lanes [19]. The B10 rebuild at the Blaubeurer Tor, with a tunnel to replace the bridge by the 2030 garden show, was decided in principle in October 2021 [22], and the chamber of commerce voiced concern in March 2025 about it and asked the city to avoid further lane cuts near the station [23]. Tram Line 2 to the university district was scheduled to open on 9 December 2018 [20].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
The garage operator, Ulmer Parkbetriebs-GmbH, raised prices on 1 May 2025. The short-term rate rose from €2.00 to €2.20 an hour in six garages, and the daily maximum from €18 to €20, and from €9 to €10 at CongressCentrumNord, with rising operating and energy costs given as the reason [4][5]. The Fischerviertel garage was closed from 3 March to 28 May 2025 for roadway renovation [11]. Surface parking was then €2.50 an hour [5].

The main new supply came from the Sedelhöfe development next to the station. The 501-space Sedelhof underground garage closed in February 2013 to make way for it [13], and the project was described in 2019 as having a new garage of 700 spaces [14]. The quarter was handed over in July 2020, with vacancies still common [15]. Blautalcenter's owner has planned to cut retail and keep its underground parking, which is a plan [16]. Five garages have EV charging, with 93 points in total [7], and the ParkenUlm app shows free spaces in real time [9]. For visitors, the tourism site recommends park-and-ride at Science Park II, Donauhalle and Kuhberg Schulzentrum, the last on Saturdays only [21].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Ulmer Parkbetriebsgesellschaft runs seven public garages, plus Kornhaus for city staff and Spitalhof for permit holders. The daily maximum is €20 on weekdays and €5 on Sundays [6]. Other garages belong to other operators: Sedelhöfe (676 spaces) to B+B Parkhaus, Frauenstraße (770) to MSDU and Congress Centrum Süd (234) to the Maritim Hotel [8]. Our measured set is six of its garages, with 2,510 spaces: Deutschhaus (596), Am Rathaus (558), Salzstadel (511), Congress Centrum Nord (400), Fischerviertel (371) and the 74-space Theater garage. Five are within 500 m of the Münsterplatz.

Occupancy over August to early October 2026 averaged 38% on weekdays and 38% at weekends. The fullest are Am Rathaus (52% on weekdays, 58% at weekends), Salzstadel (46%) and Fischerviertel (44%, 51% at weekends). Deutschhaus is at 26%, Congress Centrum Nord at 21% (5% at weekends) and the Theater garage at 20%. The five garages within 500 m average 41%.

Our history has a gap for 2024 and 2025. Between 2020 and 2023 occupancy in the same garages rose, for example at Am Rathaus from 41% to 58% and at Fischerviertel from 30% to 49%. In 2026 so far Am Rathaus stands at 53% and Fischerviertel at 46%. The Theater and Congress Centrum Nord garages were at 62% and 60% in 2023 and are at 18% and 15% in 2026 so far, and we do not know why. The data cover the summer holidays, so term-time figures may differ.
